I give up. I did not change `/work/putnam_2009_b4.lean`, and it still contains the `sorry`.

The stated answer checks out. Write P = Σ_d P_d as a sum of homogeneous parts. Then the average over the circle of radius r is Σ_d r^d · g_d, where g_d = ∫₀^{2π} P_d(cos t, sin t) dt. So P is balanced iff every g_d vanishes. For odd d, g_d = 0 always, by the symmetry t ↦ t+π. For even d, g_d is one nontrivial linear condition. Degree-≤2009 polynomials have dimension 2021055, and the 1005 even degrees 0, 2, …, 2008 each cut one dimension. That gives 2021055 − 1005 = 2020050.

The formal proof needs roughly these pieces, none of which I have built or checked:
- Lean facts: the homogeneous-component decomposition and its evaluation under scaling; interchanging the integral with a finite sum; the vanishing argument for Σ a_d r^d = 0 for all r > 0; the odd-degree symmetry; a monomial basis count for the degree-≤2009 subspace; and rank–nullity with surjectivity onto ℝ^1005, witnessed by (x²+y²)^{d/2}.

Each of these needs Mathlib lemma names I could not confirm, since only compiled Mathlib is available. Finishing would take a long, iterative development, which I did not complete.
